ZZ TEST CODE (SYNTHETIC). This text was written for software tests. It is not the law of any place.

Sec. 1.1. A health care provider shall not bill a victim for any part of a sexual assault forensic examination.
Sec. 1.2. The state examination fund pays the full cost of a sexual assault forensic examination.
Sec. 1.3. The county pays for treatment of physical injuries given within 72 hours after the victim first arrives for care.
Sec. 1.4. The total award on a claim shall not exceed $25,000.
Sec. 1.5. No award under any program in this title shall exceed $30,000.
Sec. 1.6. Counseling is reimbursed at not more than $80 per session, for up to 40 sessions.
Sec. 1.7. Counseling costs on a claim shall not exceed $3,000.
Sec. 1.8. Lost wages are paid at not more than $400 per week.
Sec. 1.9. Relocation costs shall not exceed $2,000.
Sec. 1.10. Residential security costs shall not exceed $1,000 per residence.
Sec. 1.11. Transportation to treatment is reimbursed at $0.50 per mile.
Sec. 1.12. Temporary housing is covered for up to 30 days.
Sec. 1.13. Crime scene cleanup shall not exceed $5,000 per crime scene.
Sec. 1.14. Counseling by a peer counselor is reimbursed at not more than $15 per hour.
Sec. 1.20. The program may pay reasonable medical expenses.
Sec. 1.21. The program may pay for counseling.
Sec. 1.22. The program may pay lost wages.
Sec. 1.23. The program may pay for transportation to treatment.
Sec. 1.24. The program may pay relocation costs.
Sec. 1.25. The program may pay for prescriptions.
Sec. 1.26. The program may pay dental costs.
Sec. 1.27. The program may pay childcare costs.
Sec. 1.28. The program may pay for replacement eyeglasses.
Sec. 1.30. The program shall not pay for lost or damaged personal property.
Sec. 1.31. The program shall not pay for pain and suffering.
Sec. 1.32. The program shall not pay childcare costs for a claimant who is an adult.
Sec. 1.40. A claim shall be filed within 3 years after the crime.
Sec. 1.41. A claim shall be filed within 180 days after the victim discovers the injury.
Sec. 1.42. A victim who was a minor may file within 10 years after turning eighteen.
Sec. 1.43. The board may extend a filing deadline for good cause.
Sec. 1.44. A claim based on a sexual assault may be filed within 2 years after the crime is reported to law enforcement.
Sec. 1.50. The crime shall be reported to law enforcement within 30 days, unless the victim had a sexual assault forensic examination.
Sec. 1.51. A victim does not need to report to law enforcement to receive a forensic examination.
Sec. 1.60. A claim requires an out-of-pocket loss of at least $100, which does not apply to a victim of sexual assault.
Sec. 1.61. Lost wages are paid only when the victim misses at least 5 working days.
Sec. 1.70. The program pays only after insurance and other collateral sources.
Sec. 1.71. An award may be reduced if the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
Sec. 1.72. The board may grant an emergency award of up to $1,000.
Sec. 1.73. Sexual assault is a crime covered by this title.
Sec. 1.74. Residents of ZZ and people injured by a crime in ZZ may apply.
